title: CODES golden corpus scenario
$comment: CONVENTION, as for tournament.schema.json: every object definition states additionalProperties explicitly and the default is false. The corpus is the specification of the engine, so its envelope is closed on purpose: a field nobody declared is a field no port will implement. The one open value is a patch op's `value`, which is a CODES fragment and is validated against tournament.schema.json by the writer, not here. corpusSchemaConvention.test.ts enforces this.
description: One scenario: an initial CODES tournament record, a sequence of engine directives, and after each directive the result the engine returned and the state it left, as an RFC 6902 patch against the previous canonical state plus a SHA-256 of the whole canonical state. Canonical means RFC 8785. A consumer replays the directives through its own implementation and compares hashes after id-normalisation (README.md).

factoryVersion.description: The tods-competition-factory version that produced this scenario.

schemaWriteMode.description: The write mode the engine was in. Records are native unless a scenario says otherwise.

knownFailure.description: Present when the scenario pins behaviour the engine is KNOWN to get wrong. The value is the tracker reference. A port is not graded against a known failure; a fix is a corpus update, not a drift.

invariants.description: Every invariant that must hold on the state after EVERY step. Names are defined in INVARIANTS.md.

properties.description: Relational properties the scenario was checked against. Names are defined in INVARIANTS.md.

ref.description: What to run or read to regenerate: a seed and config, a matrix cell name, a fixture filename, a test path and title.

record.description: A CODES tournamentRecord in canonical key order. Validated against tournament.schema.json by the writer; this schema only requires an object.

Hash.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical text of the state, hex, lowercase.

patch.description: RFC 6902 operations from the previous canonical state to this one. Empty when a directive was refused and changed nothing.

params.description: The params the engine consumed, ids included. A port that generates its own ids resolves them through `coordinates`.

Coordinates.description: Structural address of the matchUp a directive targets, for a port whose ids differ: which structure, which round, which position.

Result.description: What the engine returned, reduced to what a port can reproduce: exactly one of a success or a refusal, plus the context keys the corpus pins.

error.description: An error code from errorConditionConstants, e.g. MATCHUP_NOT_FOUND.

value.$comment: OPEN by necessity: a CODES fragment of any shape. Validated by the writer against tournament.schema.json where the path lands on a declared definition.
